title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Implementation status
text:
Implementation status
Implemented in [PJ-09](implementation-plan.md#current-work) on 2026-10-19, increments 1 and 2:
The [`media` API module](../../apps/api/src/features/media/AGENTS.md), its reviewed migration (which also lets profiles delegate the media capabilities), runtime grants and schema metadata, the binary upload and content operations in the [OpenAPI document](../generated/api/openapi.json), and the `TELUNI_MEDIA_` settings. Without `TELUNI_MEDIA_STORAGE_PATH` the module stays unmounted.
`media.view`, `media.upload`, `media.archive` and `media.delete` in the standard roles and as delegable profile capabilities (except `media.delete`).
The in-process processor with leases, FFmpeg isolation and renditions; delete to trash, restore, discard, purge with reference guards and object sharing, and maintenance of expired uploads, work files and orphan objects. Programming and publications register their guards in PJ-10 and PJ-11.
The [two-company integration suite](../../apps/api/test/media/integration.test.ts) processes generated fixtures with real FFmpeg against PostgreSQL as the runtime role, and [domain tests](../../apps/api/test/media/domain.test.ts) cover the bounds and the playback-profile decision.
The panel's **Mídia** pages in `apps/web` for the library, upload with per-file progress, preview, rename and tags, archive, trash and discard, with browser component tests and a [browser journey](../../apps/web/test/e2e/media/library.spec.ts) through the real identity stack and FFmpeg.
Backup consistency (2026-10-22, [deployment design](deployment-design.md#backups-and-restore)): every object file deletion first takes the `teluni.media-backup` advisory lock shared without waiting, and leaves the file for the orphan sweep while a backup holds it exclusively.
Pending: increment 3 (explicit sharing with selected branches and storage accounting for PJ-27) and a processing-timeout fixture.

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-19 under [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23):
**Storage (ADR-0028).** Media on a configured local directory behind a media-owned object interface; immutable objects named by SHA-256 per company, deduplicated only within a company; atomic publish by rename under a database lock; the database is the authority; a free-space reserve of max(2 GiB, 10%).
**Processing tool and isolation (ADR-0028).** FFmpeg 6.1 or later as an external executable for probing, image and video renditions, run as child processes with no shell, a scrubbed environment, file-only protocol, forced demuxers, timeouts and optional `prlimit`; no image library inside the API process; an in-process PostgreSQL-leased processor with concurrency 1 by default.
**Accepted inputs.** Images JPEG, PNG and static WebP; videos in MP4/MOV or Matroska/WebM with H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AV1 or MPEG-4 Part 2 video and AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC or AC-3 audio; AT-02/AT-03 bounds plus at most 8,192 px per axis and 120 fps for video.
**Playback profile.** One display rendition per asset: H.264 High 4.1, at most 1080p30, AAC-LC stereo, MP4 faststart, remuxed when already compliant; images as JPEG or PNG within 3840×2160 with orientation applied and all metadata removed; originals kept but never sent to screens. Higher profiles only with device evidence.
**Upload transport.** A create request that admits the upload, then one streamed `PUT` of the whole file with an exact declared size; no resumable protocol now.
**Scope and permissions.** Company or single-branch ownership; `media.view`, `media.upload`, `media.archive` and `media.delete` as in the table, with `media.delete` administrators only and not delegable; explicit multi-branch sharing in a later increment.
**Lifecycle and purge.** Archive and restore; delete only from archive, blocked by protected references through registered guards; 30-day trash with restore; purge rechecks references and deletes objects no other asset uses; unusable uploads discarded immediately.
**Abuse limits.** 5 open uploads per person and 20 per company, 200 creations per company per day, 20 processing per company.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Unfinished uploads discarded after one hour; rejected and failed assets kept until discarded; deleted assets purged no earlier than 30 days after deletion; purged rows and audit kept with the company.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-09 in local and CI environments with generated fixtures. It does not qualify any device profile (PH-08), select malware scanning or moderation (PH-13), or build the production image (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Media Library Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**`sharp` (libvips) for images.** Fast and well maintained, but it parses untrusted images inside the API process and adds a native dependency next to FFmpeg, which the videos need anyway. FFmpeg 6.1 applies EXIF orientation and strips metadata, so one isolated tool covers both kinds.
**Object storage (S3-compatible, for example MinIO) now.** It would separate storage from the host, but adds a service to operate on a single-host pilot with no budget. ADR-0021 already keeps the interface replaceable.
**Storing media in PostgreSQL large objects.** Transactional, but it inflates backups and database I/O with gigabytes of video and makes range reads and streaming harder.
**Global deduplication across companies.** Saves space but lets one company infer that another holds a given file and couples tenant deletion; per-company deduplication keeps tenants independent.
**Resumable uploads (tus) now.** Better for unstable connections, but adds a protocol and its state; deferred until measurements show the need.
**Sending originals to screens and relying on device decoders.** Avoids conversion, but makes playback depend on every device's codec support, which FR-04 and the release policies rule out.
**A separate processing service or queue broker.** Stronger isolation and scaling, but the pilot runs one process on one host (ADR-0021); child processes with timeouts and limits give isolation now, and a separate container is the deployment-level step in PJ-13.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Scope and acceptance rules
text:
Scope and acceptance rules
**Decided:** complete the company-to-screen journey with tenant-safe remote management, images/videos, configurable data catalogs, freeform simultaneous content, regional schedules, offline Android TV playback and monitoring. The owner prioritizes intended product capability/quality over reducing scope solely to fit an MVP label. The historical `mvp.md` path remains the stable requirements entry point.
Every capability below is a requirement, not implemented functionality. The [plan](implementation-plan.md) owns delivery status; [release policies](release-policies.md) own business behavior and the questionnaire decision record; [acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals. PH-09 policy/target selection is complete as of 2026-10-18. No hardware, pilot or performance qualification is inferred.
ID
Functional requirement
Required acceptance evidence before release
FR-01
Companies, branches, users, company settings, public company signup/automatic activation, authentication, scoped standard/custom profiles and temporary access
Two synthetic companies each have branches/users. Authorized members manage allowed resources; direct API attempts, lists/search, media/catalog access and identifier substitution cannot cross company/branch scope. Verify responsible-administrator approval, trusted account linking, strong/recent authentication, recovery, session bounds and 30-second revocation using [IA-01–IA-16](identity-and-access.md#required-verification-cases). Public activation must satisfy commercial/privacy/abuse gates; platform operation has no implicit customer-content access.
FR-02
Device identity, temporary-code pairing, company/branch assignment, name/configuration and safe unlink
An authorized user claims a displayed code once. Expired/replayed codes, concurrent claims, wrong-scope assignment and revoked identities fail safely. Reassignment requires verified cleanup/reset and cannot expose previous tenant data/credentials; unreachable erasure is shown as pending.
FR-03
Supported horizontal/vertical orientation
Qualified devices display supported orientations correctly; invalid geometry or unsupported profiles have explicit outcomes rather than silent support claims.
FR-04
Private image/video upload, validation, organization, metadata, reuse, conversion and reference-aware deletion
Approved profiles upload, validate/convert and play on tested hardware. Spoofed type, malformed/oversized content and unauthorized reads fail safely. Archive/deletion/retention preserve protected draft, active, staging and recovery references; assisted draft changes need confirmation.
FR-05
Playlists, ordered items, configurable image duration, full-video playback, looping, device/group assignment and qualified cuts/fades
Deterministic order and preview/player duration agreement. Devices have zero or one company-owned group, including cross-branch groups; explicit individual programming replaces the whole group source. Confirmed source changes use published content or an intentionally empty destination. Ordinary item completion and coordinated-page timing follow release policies.
FR-06
Dates, local hours, weekdays, overnight recurrence, regional schedules and deterministic conflict/no-match rules
Shared backend/player fixtures cover inclusive starts/exclusive ends, final-date clipping, all-day/equal-time validation, timezone/DST, overlapping same-output windows, regional exceptions and empty windows. Optional defaults otherwise give safe neutral output; expired commercial content is not an implicit fallback.
FR-07
Preview, publication, immutable consistent versions, desired/downloaded/active state and last-valid preservation
Ordinary drafts do not affect screens. Authorized price saves automatically publish affected published bindings through durable/retry-safe intent, excluding unrelated drafts. Concurrent/repeated operations and unknown outcomes are reconcilable. Complete supported versions activate only after validated staging; failures never replace valid state with mixed/corrupt resources.
FR-08
Android TV playback, bounded offline operation and controlled recovery/update
Qualified devices play local media/catalog snapshots without normal backend streaming, through the selected offline/clock/authorization envelope, reboot, power interruption and protocol/update cases in playback acceptance. Expired authorization or untrusted time has an explicit safe outcome.
FR-09
Scoped connection/last-contact/app/storage/sync/playback diagnostics
Show observed timestamps, stale/offline thresholds and actual version states. Distinguish failed sync, regional rendering failure and lost contact from stopped playback. Reconnection reconciles state without leaking data or claiming unseen erasure.
FR-10
Freeform simultaneous composition, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, per-area schedules, multiple videos and configurable mixed audio
Users position/resize areas and preview copy/import/export of versioned textual layouts. An active regional schedule survives a global page change; coordinated areas follow the selected page timeline. Isolated area failure/no-match preserves unaffected geometry/output. Qualified rendering/audio profiles and pagination remain readable and work offline.
FR-11
User-defined typed catalogs, fields and records with layout bindings, including products/prices and weekly agendas
Users configure a non-product catalog as well as a product configuration. Validate schema/version evolution, scoped record/media references, branch price overrides and import boundaries. Data-driven views paginate without silent name/price clipping. Price publication/expiry and unavailable-item defaults work from consistent offline snapshots; customization cannot execute arbitrary code or cross tenant boundaries.
FR-12
Bounded public trial, contracted screen licenses, qualified quota admission and manually administered commercial authorization
[CP-01–CP-12](commercial-policies.md#required-commercial-verification) cover verified trial boundaries, fixed licenses/replacement, reserved capacity, safe expiry/grace/cancellation/export and separately authorized payment reconciliation. No billing from heartbeat, partial download cutoff, unlimited defaults, surprise charge or security-suspension bypass. PH-18/PH-19 qualify the offer; no gateway or automatic invoicing is required.
Managed campaigns remain future scope; scheduled content and published price-validity rules provide the initial promotion behavior without approving a separate campaign engine.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Release acceptance journey
text:
Release acceptance journey
Establish two synthetic companies through verified enrollment with responsible administrators, differently scoped branches/operators and qualified Android TV devices. Exercise IA-01–IA-16 login/linking/recovery/session/revocation/approval/support cases and API/media/catalog allow/deny boundaries; no implicit platform content privilege.
Pair devices, create a cross-branch group and an explicit individual exception. Upload media; configure a custom weekly-agenda catalog and product/price configuration. Compose independent and coordinated areas, regional schedules and an optional default; preview and publish A.
Verify local multi-video/audio/catalog rendering under the qualified profile. Edit drafts without changing A. Save a price and verify automatic consistent publication from published dependencies without leaking unrelated drafts; test concurrent edits, duplicate delivery and failed/unknown outcomes.
Publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at download/staging/activation boundaries and verify complete valid A or B. Isolate a runtime regional fault without confusing it with incomplete-generation activation. Check protected references and insufficient disk outcomes.
Exercise schedule/date/DST/promotion/no-match/pagination and regional-page timing offline. Test the trusted-clock and authorization deadlines, restart/recovery and the expected safe neutral states.
Reconnect and reconcile observed state. Unlink/revoke while offline, then verify cleanup before cross-company pairing. Exercise historical recovery without expired offers or resurrected credentials and validate controlled protocol/app updates.
Exercise CP-01–CP-12 commercial trial/license/quota, reconciled-payment and grace/cancellation cases, preserving independent identity permission and valid offline deadlines. Rehearse database-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in isolation. Record target-linked load/usability/hardware evidence, customer acceptance, real costs/support coverage and residual risk before real-customer acceptance; billing readiness remains PH-19.
Evidence includes automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, representative hardware/power/network tests, restore results and user observation. Delivery can be incremental; an operational release requires the complete applicable acceptance set. Passing foundation validation only checks currently implemented foundation/docs.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Explicitly outside the MVP
text:
Explicitly outside the MVP
The historical heading remains a stable route; initial scope now includes freeform composition, configurable catalogs and their approved commercial defaults. Further unreviewed widgets, managed campaigns, external ERP/POS/partner integration APIs/webhooks/imports, automated billing/payment-gateway subscriptions, white-label, AI, playback analytics, general remote-control tools, impersonation, synchronization across separate screens and alternative players remain future unless independently approved. PH-11 separately selects scoped consent-based human support, custom access profiles and optional independent publication approvals for the initial release; custom profiles exist for the current organization capabilities, and the other policies remain unimplemented. Generic fields do not approve arbitrary executable plugins, unrestricted data collection or all roadmap capabilities.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Constraints and current state
text:
Constraints and current state
**Decided constraint:** no present cloud-service budget. The owner intends to use a personal residential server for development, tests and potentially initial customers, moving to a VPS/cloud when revenue or operational need justifies it. **Accepted initial architecture under ADR-0021:** Debian Linux, Docker Compose, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, local persistent media, automated backups and suitable monitoring. Real-customer use remains subject to PH-10 readiness gates. None is a deployed Teluni environment or executable procedure in this repository. On 2026-10-22 the [pilot deployment and recovery design](deployment-design.md) and ADR-0033 decided, under the owner's delegation, the exposure path, proxy, composition, backups and recovery targets that PJ-13 builds.
Follow inherited [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets management](../security/secrets-management.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [observability](../reliability/observability.md), [alerting](../reliability/alerting.md), and [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md). This plan does not grant production authority. Write tested deployment/recovery runbooks when the environment exists, rather than speculative commands now.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Residential exposure and readiness gate
text:
Residential exposure and readiness gate
[PH-10](human-actions.md#ph-10) requires an actual host/network inventory: CPU/RAM/disk and growth, upload bandwidth, data caps, power/reboot recovery, router/firewall, public address or CGNAT, ISP restrictions, available domain, certificate renewal, secure remote administration and backup connectivity. Keep private addresses, credentials and sensitive topology out of tracked public documentation.
A tunnel, free DNS option or any video-delivery intermediary requires evaluation of current terms, limits, privacy, security, transfer cost and failure behavior before selection. Do not assume Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS, or video distribution automatically provides an acceptable production path. The [deployment design](deployment-design.md#reaching-the-residential-host) evaluated them and selects end-to-end TLS on the host, reached directly or through a TCP relay that never terminates TLS.
Before any real pilot, record and demonstrate:
HTTPS works end to end; only intentional public application endpoints are exposed. PostgreSQL, orchestration dashboards and administrative interfaces remain private/restricted. Remote administration does not imply an unrestricted remote-control product feature.
Development/test and customer data, identities, credentials and backups are separated; logs/diagnostics are redacted; real data does not enter development fixtures.
Durable database and media survive container recreation, controlled app updates and host reboot. Schema migrations use reviewed release procedures and an explicit recovery plan.
Offline playback has been tested independently from backend availability. A home outage still prevents new uploads, publication, pairing, current monitoring and some recovery; communicate these limits to pilot participants.
The owner agrees measurable availability, maintenance, incident contact, backup RPO/RTO and support expectations. Availability, maintenance and RPO/RTO are decided in the [deployment design](deployment-design.md#recovery-and-availability-targets); incident contact and support coverage remain PH-18. [Commercial policies](commercial-policies.md) select no initial formal availability SLA; actual support coverage and cost/capacity evidence remain PH-18. Do not advertise the delegated example paid quotas as measured host capacity. No commercial SLA is implied by the architecture.
Until verified, external exposure and real-customer operation are **pending**, even if development works locally.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Persistent state and storage portability
text:
Persistent state and storage portability
Keep environment-specific URLs, credentials and paths in validated environment configuration; use only implemented keys from the [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md) today. Define and document new keys with their future canonical schemas when implemented. Do not embed the residential hostname/path in business entities, contracts or player binaries.
**Accepted storage boundary:** the media capability owns object identity, integrity, metadata, authorized reads and lifecycle. Isolate the actual filesystem I/O behind a cohesive media-owned storage responsibility so a future S3-compatible implementation can preserve object semantics without rewriting domain rules. Avoid a general provider framework or mandatory S3 dependency now. Object-store replacement still needs verified access, integrity, migration and concurrency semantics; portability is not a free automatic migration.
Use durable logical object identifiers rather than storing temporary download credentials as business identity. External media endpoints are configurable. Authorized delivery may use an API or another reviewed access mechanism; public filesystem paths and unbounded permanent bearer URLs are not the default.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Backup and restore requirements
text:
Backup and restore requirements
Backups must cover PostgreSQL, media, future provider identity state and the non-secret configuration/release metadata needed to reconstruct operation. Review future session persistence separately: restoring old sessions must never resurrect revoked access; session invalidation/reauthentication may be necessary. Provider signing material and authentication recovery require a protected, separately controlled recovery path, not plaintext configuration exports. Protect and recover secrets through a separate controlled process. A database-only backup is insufficient if it points to unavailable media.
Choose a consistency method for the database-plus-files set, backup schedule, off-host destination, encryption/key recovery, retention, capacity and success/failure reporting. A second directory on the same disk does not cover loss of the host. Local budget constraints do not eliminate the need to resolve off-host recovery before accepting private customer data.
Rehearse restore into an isolated environment: verify migration/application compatibility, ownership/permissions, manifest-to-file integrity, representative playback and tenant access, then reconcile revoked identities and deletion/retention obligations. Record achieved recovery point/time and compare them with owner-approved RPO/RTO. Preserve audit/release history; do not restore stale authorization silently.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Future host or storage migration
text:
Future host or storage migration
**Proposed sequence**, to turn into tested runbooks once topology and credentials exist:
Inventory supported player versions, configurable API/media addresses, tenant data, assets, release versions and secret destinations. Prepare DNS/certificate ownership and compatible software at the destination.
Rehearse backup restore and file verification without customer writes. Determine whether logical object IDs remain stable and how private media authorization is preserved.
Plan a bounded write cutover or verified incremental reconciliation to avoid divergent metadata and media. Preserve audit and device identities without exposing their credentials.
Update endpoints through the approved mechanism with certificate validation and rollback capability. Keep the old address/redirect or compatibility path only for an explicitly defined overlap, accounting for long-offline players. Never accept arbitrary redirected credential recipients.
Verify representative players reconnect, reconcile desired/active versions, and continue offline playback. Check uploads, access denial, publication, backups and monitoring on the new host.
Close the rollback window deliberately, reconcile retained data/deletions and retire old storage/credentials safely. The endpoint overlap and maximum supported offline interval must be compatible; unresolved unreachable devices require a support plan.
Commercial admission must budget originals plus renditions/protected history/staging/backups, aggregate traffic/control work and conversion concurrency. PH-12 policy selection does not authorize unlimited public trials or new recurring procurement; PH-18/PJ-27 require measured safe quotas before admission.
Triggers for migration include measured cost/availability/support risk, storage or uplink saturation, growth, or earned revenue supporting operations. Cloud procurement and live migration are outside this documentation task.

text:
Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
[Requirements](mvp.md) · [Release policies](release-policies.md) · [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) · [ADR-0019 decision](../adr/0019-propose-immutable-publications-and-atomic-player-activation.md)

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Required guarantees and implementation boundary
text:
Required guarantees and implementation boundary
**Decided requirements:** local media and catalog rendering through the bounded offline envelope, integrity validation, complete-generation activation and last-valid recovery. Normal video playback does not stream repeatedly from the backend. Freeform composition, independently scheduled areas with optional page coordination, multiple videos/audio and typed custom catalogs must meet the same obligations.
PH-09 has selected product behavior and numeric qualification targets. Protocol/schema serialization, integrity metadata/algorithms, local transactions/storage, processing/rendering libraries, transport and credential/trusted-time mechanisms remain engineering review under D-03/D-04/D-05/D-07/D-11. [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-propose-versioned-catalog-and-composition-publications.md) establishes the accepted versioned catalog/composition boundary; neither ADR is an implemented protocol or evidence of durability.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Publication lifecycle
text:
Publication lifecycle
An authorized publisher deliberately publishes ordinary draft state. A designated price save instead automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings under the release policies; it does not release unrelated layout/schema/record drafts.
Validate actor/target tenant and branch scope, schema/record/field bindings, compatible rendering/media profiles, scheduling, effective prices and durable media. Build an immutable complete snapshot with the rules/data needed for offline interpretation. Desired availability must not precede durable assets and metadata.
Record the desired generation and required work durably. A database update and media filesystem writes are not one transaction. Stage/verify objects, then commit references/intent with recoverable cleanup and reconciliation. Follow delivery policy; an in-memory after-commit callback alone cannot guarantee price/publication fan-out.
The independently authenticated device reconciles its authorized desired generation and local active/staged state. It receives only compatible tenant-scoped rules, schema/record snapshots and media descriptors. A content path is not immutable identity when its bytes can change.
Preflight space for staged plus protected active/recovery resources and the target reserve, counting shared files once. Download absent/changed assets with bounded timeouts/retries. Interrupted files cannot masquerade as complete; refreshing download authorization cannot make private media public.
Verify expected length/integrity, references, schema interpretation and renderer/media capability before accepting resources. A checksum detects corruption but does not authenticate an untrusted manifest by itself. Preserve valid active output on invalid or incomplete staging.
Prepare the complete supported local generation, then durably activate it. Keep publication selection distinct from the schedule that chooses its eligible output. Atomic-generation recovery and safe resource release need actual power-cut tests; do not overwrite active files progressively.
Report desired, received/staged and reported-active facts separately. Repeated/lost acknowledgements must reconcile; server acceptance is not proof of TV activation. The panel represents active A plus failed staging B without calling every sync failure a playback outage.
Retain the previous valid generation and protected staging resources under retention/reference rules. Restore only if still authorized, compatible and commercially valid. Do not resurrect expired promotions, deleted ownership or revoked credentials.
Confirmed assignment/source changes use the latest published programming without another content publish action. An explicitly confirmed destination with no first publication produces authorized neutral no-programming output after the assignment is applied. This deliberate empty source differs from failed/corrupt synchronization, which preserves valid state. An unreachable player cannot apply an unseen assignment or erasure.
Candidate logical states such as unpaired, no-content, staging, active, degraded and pending-clear describe concurrent facts, not committed enum/API names. Their exact schema must preserve the distinctions above.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Consistency and concurrency
text:
Consistency and concurrency
Publication/price-save/download/acknowledgement operations need explicit idempotency, stale-write detection, retry ownership, bounded attempts and observable failure/reconciliation. Do not treat a mutation timeout as certain failure or retry an unprotected side effect.
Order desired state using authoritative generation/revision information, not device wall-clock order. Old acknowledgements and stale processing cannot roll a target back to an earlier price or assignment.
Under the owner's delegation, prefer the latest authorized compatible desired snapshot and permit coalescing superseded pending delivery work. Keep attributable publication/price history and every still-valid schedule in the latest snapshot; coalescing delivery is not deleting audit events or omitting future programmed transitions.
Use published dependency revisions for automatic price publication. Concurrent schema/layout drafts remain separate. Expose saved/queued/publication-failed states, reconcile incomplete fan-out and never claim successful device distribution from the catalog transaction alone.
Typed schema evolution/import and reference validation are part of publication validity. A record/field reference cannot bypass tenant/branch authorization or select another tenant through a custom value.
Retry elapsed time is separate from business scheduling. Respect application shutdown and bounded work claims; a crashed worker must not lose required intent or leave inaccessible staging permanently.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Time and regional scheduling
text:
Time and regional scheduling
[Release policies](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling) own the exact calendar/DST/overnight/date-clipping and conflict rules. Backend preview and player must share fixtures for them, regional overrides/page coordination, promotional price validity, pagination and no-match output. Store/compare instants while retaining the geographic zone needed for recurring local time; never inherit the backend host timezone.
An active regional schedule controls its area's output even while the underlying page changes. On ending, return to the applicable current-page/default/neutral state without restarting independent areas. Coordinated page-controlled participants use a common transition point; ordinary short-video completion holds the last frame while the page continues. Schedule boundaries interrupt affected output and override fades/page/item completion without extending expired content.
A regional rendering failure inside an active valid generation may use its still-valid local contingency or neutral area and report degradation while other areas continue. This runtime isolation does not permit activation of a publication with missing/corrupt required resources. A recovered coordinated area rejoins the current valid page/schedule state; it does not replay expired content or reset every area.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
text:
Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
The [target specification](release-targets.md#reliability-and-synchronization-targets) defines offline authorization and trusted-clock limits. Authorization expiry gives neutral output and requires reconnection; a restored cache cannot extend it. Server revocation rejects new protected operations while a disconnected cache may persist until local authorization expires. Erasure is pending until actually observed, and another tenant cannot pair before verified cleanup/reset.
Detectable clock jumps or insufficient trusted-time confidence suspend time-dependent schedules/prices. Do not claim an incorrect wall clock can always be detected without a reference. If remaining authorization validity cannot be established safely, protected playback must also stop; a local setup/neutral view does not disclose private tenant data. Reboot/offline time estimation and established credential/cryptographic components require threat-model review and qualified tests before delivery.
Initial pairing/synchronization requires backend access. With no valid installed program show safe local setup/no-content output. A publication's optional default or neutral fallback is evaluated locally within authorization and content-validity rules, not permission to replay stale commercial data indefinitely.

Failure and recovery acceptance
Condition

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Decided detailed design for D-07, 2026-10-20.** The owner delegated every pending decision to the agent on 2026-10-20 (recorded with [PH-25](human-actions.md#ph-25)). The agent took the [decisions](#decisions) below under that delegation, together with ADR-0031. Merging the pull request that adds this design is the repository review. The decisions authorize [PJ-12](implementation-plan.md#current-work) in local and CI environments. They do not qualify any device: hardware support, timings and power-loss behavior remain [PH-08](human-actions.md#ph-08) and PJ-14 evidence.
In scope: the player's components and build, installation and unattended operation, enrollment and credential storage on the device, synchronization, staging, activation and recovery, local storage, trusted time, enforcement of the authorization statement, schedule evaluation and playback of protocol 1 publications, orientation, neutral and setup output, erasure, updates and compatibility, diagnostics, the additions this needs in the sync response, and verification (FR-02, FR-03, FR-07, FR-08, NF-08).
Out of scope, with their owners: freeform areas, coordinated pages, multiple videos and audio mixing (PJ-20, D-11) and catalog views (PJ-21), which extend the manifest in a later protocol and reuse this player's storage, time and authorization; diagnostic uploads and alerts (D-09); commercial capping of authorization (PJ-27); the update channel's server-side release management and the production host (PJ-13); fades, which stay refused until a device profile qualifies them (PH-08).

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these policies without changing them:
Activate only a complete, verified generation; keep the active and previous valid generations and a valid staging attempt; preserve a free reserve of at least max(1 GiB, 10% of the volume) after planned use; refuse unsafe staging without deleting protected resources (ADR-0019, AT-05, AT-19).
First cached output within 10 seconds after the OS starts the player, process recovery within 30 seconds, reboot to content within 120 seconds, and no mixed or incomplete active generation over at least 20 power cuts (AT-06 to AT-09).
Seven days of offline playback with reboots, then neutral output at authorization expiry; trusted-time uncertainty of at most 60 seconds; detected incompatible clock jumps or an insufficient time reference suspend time-dependent output (AT-10, AT-15, AT-16).
Detect a desired publication within 30 seconds, activate within 5 seconds once resources are verified, and change scheduled output within 500 ms of a boundary (AT-11 to AT-13).
Per-device local business time with explicit IANA zones, inclusive starts and exclusive ends, the gap and repeated-hour resolutions, and fixtures shared with the backend preview ([time and scheduling](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling)).
Newly created areas start muted, and mixing audio needs deliberate configuration ([composition](release-policies.md#composition-and-regional-playback)).
Unlink requires erasure on reconnection; another company pairs a new identity only after cleanup ([device enrollment](device-enrollment-design.md#device-lifecycle)).
Controlled update distribution with a configurable window, qualified installation and recovery, and no untested app or data downgrade; support the current and previous protocol for at least 90 days after a transition (AT-26).

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Components
text:
Components
The player is a separate Gradle build in `apps/player`, outside the pnpm workspace, with two modules:
**`core`** (Kotlin on the JVM, no Android dependency): the protocol models, the manifest parser, verification of authorization statements, the schedule evaluator, trusted time, the local generation store, the synchronization engine and the playback decisions (what plays now and until when). Everything with rules lives here, so it runs as fast JVM tests in CI, including the shared fixtures.
**`app`** (Android): the activity and its screens, rendering with Media3 ExoPlayer, the Android Keystore credential vault, device-owner integration, boot and crash handling, and adapters that give `core` its clock, files and HTTP.
`core` talks to the API through OkHttp and parses JSON with kotlinx.serialization: strictly for manifests, whose format changes only with a new protocol, and ignoring unknown fields in API responses, which may gain fields compatibly. Statements are verified with Nimbus JOSE + JWT, an established implementation, restricted to `ES256`. The player never imports backend or web code; it depends on the published HTTP contracts and on the repository's shared test fixtures.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Installation and unattended operation
text:
Installation and unattended operation
Two installation profiles. PH-08 records which one each device model supports:
**Managed (the supported profile for the pilot).** On a factory-reset device, an installer sideloads the APK and makes the player the device owner with `adb shell dpm set-device-owner`. The player is then the HOME activity and runs in lock task mode. It keeps the screen on while powered, disables the keyguard, starts at boot as the launcher, is relaunched by the system after a crash, and installs its updates without a confirmation prompt.
**Basic.** The APK is sideloaded and chosen as the default HOME app where the device allows it. Updates need someone at the screen to confirm them. This profile counts as unattended only when PH-08 shows that it starts at boot and recovers from crashes on that model.
The activity is the only user interface. Each update and process start goes through the same startup sequence:
Read the state record and the stored statement.
Start output from the active generation, or neutral or setup output, within AT-06's 10 seconds.
Start synchronizing.
An uncaught exception is recorded locally (code and stack frames of the player only, never content or credentials) before the process ends. In the managed profile the system restarts the HOME activity, which AT-07 qualifies.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Supported hardware envelope
text:
Supported hardware envelope
Decided on 2026-10-22 under the owner's delegation (the decision part of [PH-08](human-actions.md#ph-08)). This is the envelope that devices are bought and qualified against. Only PH-08 measurements on a real model make that model supported.
**Platform.** Android TV OS or Google TV, certified by Google (Play Protect certified) and homologated by Anatel, running Android 9 or later. `minSdk` stays 26, but Android 8 devices are not bought for the pilot because their security updates have ended. Smart TVs on other systems (Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku) and Fire OS are outside the envelope. On those TVs an HDMI device inside the envelope is used instead.
**Uncertified "TV box" devices** sold without Anatel homologation are excluded, even when they run Android. They often ship with modified firmware and preinstalled malware, which the device credential cannot protect against.
**Form.** The pilot's reference class is a Google TV HDMI streaming device (for example a Xiaomi TV Box S, second generation), which works with whatever TV the customer already has. A TV with Google TV built in is qualified separately per model.
**Minimums.** 2 GB of RAM, 8 GB of storage with at least 4 GB free for the media store after setup, hardware decoding of H.264 High 4.1 at 1080p30 with AAC, and 1080p HDMI output.
**Network.** Ethernet where the installation allows it (through a USB adapter on sticks), otherwise 5 GHz Wi-Fi. Playback needs no bandwidth once a generation is staged; staging time grows with media size.
**Installation.** The device must allow the managed profile: a factory reset, then `adb` over the network or USB to set the device owner before any Google account is added.
**Orientation.** Landscape at 0 and 180 degrees on every model. Portrait (90 and 270) only on models where PH-08 shows the rotation works with hardware decoding.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Enrollment and credential
text:
Enrollment and credential
The player follows the [device enrollment design](device-enrollment-design.md):
It generates a 256-bit credential with `SecureRandom` and starts an enrollment with its SHA-256 and the device report: app version, protocols, manufacturer, model, OS version, display size and supported rotations.
It shows the code as `XXXX-XXXX` in large type with the panel address, and polls the enrollment status at the interval the server gives.
An expired code starts a new enrollment with a new credential, because a hash is never reused. Every enrollment starts from an empty store.
The credential is stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a key that Android Keystore creates and never exports. The ciphertext, IV and key alias live in an app-private file written atomically. Backup is disabled for the whole application (`allowBackup="false"` and data extraction rules that exclude everything), so neither the credential nor content leaves the device. A credential that cannot be decrypted (for example after a Keystore reset) counts as absent: the player erases its local state and enrolls again, and the panel then sees a new screen.
Erasure: when synchronization or `GET /device/self` answers `clearRequired`, the player stops protected output and any staging attempt, lets no exchange run meanwhile, and deletes media, generations, statements, keys, the state record and the credential file and Keystore key. Only then does it call `POST /device/self/erasure` with the credential it still holds in memory, and it returns to enrollment. If the confirmation fails, it retries while the process lives. A lost confirmation leaves the server's erasure pending, which the panel already shows as unconfirmed.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Synchronization
text:
Synchronization
The synchronization engine runs in the application process for as long as the player runs:
It calls `POST /device/sync` at the server's `nextSyncSeconds` (30), with the report the [publication design](publication-sync-design.md#state-reports-and-monitoring) defines.
After a failure it retries at 30 seconds, then doubles up to 2 minutes with ±20% jitter, and honors `Retry-After`. Connect and read timeouts are 10 and 30 seconds for sync, and 30 seconds of inactivity for downloads.
Each successful response updates the trusted-time anchor, the zone offsets, the rotation and the statement, in that order, before any decision uses them.
When the desired publication differs from the active one and from the staging attempt, the engine starts staging it. A newer desired publication supersedes a staging attempt at once, and an attempt for a publication that is no longer desired (for example, after the destination returns to the active publication) is forgotten with the files only it used. Files the new publication also needs are kept, which coalesces superseded work as the policies allow. Staging:
**Manifest.** Download it, check that its size and SHA-256 match `desired`, and check that the latest valid statement lists that SHA-256. Parse it strictly as protocol 1. Unknown kinds or content types, fades, or anything the player cannot interpret fail as `INVALID_MANIFEST` or `INCOMPATIBLE`.
**Preflight.** First delete the files of a superseded attempt that the active, recovery and new staging generations do not use. Then add the bytes of media not yet in the store, counting shared files once. Refuse with `STORAGE_FULL` when the free space after the download would fall below the reserve. A publication whose media are all stored needs no room, so a schedule-only change activates even on a volume that is already below the reserve. Nothing protected is deleted to make room; the report carries the bytes needed.
**Download.** Fetch the missing media, at most two at a time and at most about 85 requests a minute, into `.part` files. The API's screen routes allow 120 requests per credential and minute, so the pace always leaves room for synchronization. A `RATE_LIMITED` answer waits for its `Retry-After` (at most 60 seconds) and retries the file, up to five times. Resume with single ranges from what a `.part` file holds; the API serves an immutable rendition per media item, and the final check covers resumed bytes. Check the length and SHA-256, flush the file to disk, then rename it into the content store and flush the directory. A complete `.part` file that does not match is downloaded again from the start; freshly downloaded bytes that do not match fail the attempt as `INTEGRITY_FAILED`. A `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` on a manifest or media request means the desired publication changed: the engine synchronizes again at once instead of retrying.
**Ready.** When every file is present and verified, the attempt is `READY` and activation follows (next section). Progress is reported in bytes.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Local storage, activation and recovery
text:
Local storage, activation and recovery
All state lives in app-private internal storage. There is no database: the few records the player keeps are files that are replaced atomically, which avoids schema migrations and makes power-loss behavior easy to test.
files/
  state.json            atomically replaced: active, recovery and staging pointers, format version
  credential.bin        encrypted credential (Keystore-wrapped)
  keys.json             pinned statement keys (JWKS)
  statement.jws         latest verified statement
  sync.json             latest zone offsets, rotation, time anchor and lower bound
  generations/<publicationId>/manifest.json   exact manifest bytes
  media/<sha256>        content store, write-once, read-only
  media/<sha256>.part   download in progress

Each record is written to a temporary file, flushed with `fsync`, renamed over the old one and its directory flushed. A reader therefore sees either the old or the new record, never a mix. **Activation** is one such replacement of `state.json` that sets the staged publication active and the previous active one as recovery. It happens only when all of these hold:
the staged generation is `READY`;
its manifest is stored;
the latest valid statement lists it;
trusted time is available and the statement has not expired.
Output switches at once, like a schedule boundary (AT-12). After activation, files not referenced by the active, recovery or staging generation are deleted.
At startup, before output, the player reconciles its storage:
It removes `.part` files that do not belong to the current staging attempt and media no generation references.
It drops a pointer whose manifest file is missing.
It falls back from a broken active generation to recovery, and from there to neutral output, reporting `DEGRADED`.
Media files were verified when they entered the store, so startup checks only their presence and size, which keeps AT-06. A background scrub re-hashes one file at a time at low priority. A decoding failure re-hashes that file at once. A mismatch deletes it, and the file is downloaded again if the publication is still desired; otherwise its items are skipped and `DEGRADED` is reported.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Trusted time and zone offsets
text:
Trusted time and zone offsets
Business time never comes from the device's wall clock or time zone database alone:
**Anchor.** Each successful sync gives the server's `serverTime`. The player records it with the monotonic `elapsedRealtime` at the midpoint of the request, and the anchor's uncertainty is half the round trip. Responses with a round trip above 10 seconds do not replace a better anchor. Trusted now is the anchor's server time plus the monotonic time elapsed since. The monotonic clock keeps counting in deep sleep, and seven days of drift at a typical 50 ppm stays near 30 seconds, inside AT-16; qualification measures real devices.
**Lower bound.** Every minute, and at each anchor, the player persists the latest trusted instant.
**After a reboot without a server answer.** The monotonic clock restarts, so the anchor is lost. The player then accepts the system clock only when it is not earlier than the persisted lower bound and automatic network time is enabled. It reports the clock as estimated until the next sync. Otherwise it reports `CLOCK_UNTRUSTED` and shows neutral output until a sync succeeds. As the policies say, a wrong clock without a reference cannot always be detected; PH-08 measures the devices' real-time clock behavior.
**Jumps.** While an anchor exists, the player uses it and ignores changes to the system clock. It reports a difference between the system clock and trusted time above 60 seconds as a diagnostic.
**Zone offsets.** Many Android TV devices stay on old time zone data; for example, a device without updates since 2019 still applies daylight saving time in `America/Sao_Paulo`. The player therefore uses the server's rules: each sync response adds `zoneOffsets`, the UTC offsets of the screen's zone from three days before `serverTime` to 35 days after it, as `{ "until": instant, "periods": [{ "from": instant, "offsetSeconds": n }] }`. The API computes them with the same Temporal API its evaluator uses. Preview and player then agree by construction. Evaluation reads windows from the local day before "now", up to about 62 hours back, so three days of history suffice. The 35 days ahead cover the seven-day authorization with room for look-ahead. The player resolves local times against these periods with exactly the server's rules: a gap resolves to its transition instant, and a repeated hour to the earlier occurrence for a start and the later for an end. An instant outside the covered range has no business time, so the player reports `CLOCK_UNTRUSTED` and shows neutral output. Offsets are not signed: they arrive over authenticated TLS, and the statement, not the offsets, bounds what may play.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Authorization
text:
Authorization
The player trusts only statements it has verified:
The header must be `ES256` with `typ` `teluni-authorization+jws` and a `kid` in the pinned key set.
The signature must verify.
`sub` and `company` must be the screen's own.
`iat` must be earlier than `exp`.
Keys are pinned when the player first fetches `GET /device/keys` over TLS after pairing. A statement with an unknown `kid` triggers one fetch of the key set over TLS; a statement that still does not verify is ignored, and the previous statement stays in force until its own expiry. The player keeps only the latest verified statement. A statement older (by `iat`) than the stored one never replaces it, and nothing extends `exp` locally.
Protected output plays only while trusted time is before the stored statement's `exp` and the statement lists the manifest SHA-256 of the generation being played. An empty list, an expired statement or no statement gives neutral output: `AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED` after expiry, `NEUTRAL` for an unpublished source. This is how an assignment to an unpublished destination reaches neutral output, and how a suspended company's screens stop at the latest expiry.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Playback
text:
Playback
**What plays.** Protocol 1 has one output, `screen`. The `core` evaluator is a port of the API's evaluator and is checked against the [shared fixtures](programming-design.md#shared-fixtures). It turns the active manifest's rules and default, the zone offsets and trusted now into the current segment and the instant of the next boundary. A segment plays a rule's playlist, the default playlist or neutral output. At each boundary the output changes at once, interrupting the current item (AT-13). Boundaries are timed on the monotonic clock, and the segment is evaluated again after any anchor or offset change. When a boundary keeps the same playlist, playback continues. A new segment with a different playlist starts it at its first item.
**Rendering.** Media3 ExoPlayer plays each playlist's items in order and loops:
Images show for their `durationMs`, decoded at most at the output's size. Videos play their whole rendition.
The next item is prepared while the current one plays, so a direct cut has no visible gap; qualification measures it.
Content is fitted inside the output without distortion, on black.
Protocol 1 plays muted, because the policies start areas muted and protocol 1 has no audio setting. Audio arrives with per-area volume in the composition protocol (PJ-20).
**Orientation.** The rotation comes with each sync response and from `GET /device/self`. Rotation 0 renders on a `SurfaceView`; 90, 180 and 270 rotate the content view, which needs a `TextureView` for video, as one coordinated transform. PH-08 qualifies each rotation per model.
**Failures.** An item that fails to decode is skipped for the rest of the segment, retried at the next segment, re-verified as above and reported as `DEGRADED`. When every item of the segment fails, the output is neutral until the next boundary. A failed staging never touches the active generation.
**Neutral and setup output.** Both are black screens with the Teluni mark and no tenant content:
Setup output shows the pairing code, or a short state such as "connecting".
Neutral output shows nothing else until someone presses OK on the remote. A status card then appears for 30 seconds with the screen name, the reported state, the last contact and the app version.
Text follows the device locale, `pt-BR` or `en-US`, with `pt-BR` as the default.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Updates and compatibility
text:
Updates and compatibility
**Manifests.** The player declares its supported protocols in every sync. An incompatible manifest fails staging and keeps the active generation, and the report names the incompatibility. Protocol 2, for programs with a layout, is served beside protocol 1 rather than replacing it, so a player that supports 2 keeps supporting 1; `desired.protocol` lets an older player report `INCOMPATIBLE` without downloading. A protocol that replaces another is supported beside it for at least 90 days (AT-26).
**Local state.** `state.json` carries a format version. Each release migrates older formats forward when it starts. A format the release does not know is not read: the player keeps the credential, discards content state and synchronizes again, which costs downloads but never mixes formats.
**Releases (increment 4).** The API serves the release approved for the screen through two device operations: the release description (version code, size, SHA-256) and the APK. The player downloads it like media.
**Installation.** The player verifies the APK's SHA-256 and that its signing certificate equals the installed one. It then installs through `PackageInstaller` inside the update window, by default 03:00 to 05:00 local business time, unless a release is marked urgent. Android refuses a lower version code, so the player never downgrades.
**Rollback.** A rollback is a new release with a higher version code built from the earlier source and able to read the current state format.
**Ownership.** The release signing key is a human-held secret ([PH-27](human-actions.md#ph-27)). Release approval and the update window are operational configuration (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Diagnostics and privacy
text:
Diagnostics and privacy
The player sends nothing beyond the sync report and erasure confirmation; diagnostic uploads are D-09. Logcat output is limited to states, error codes and publication IDs. It never contains credentials, statements, manifests, media, URLs with credentials or the pairing code after pairing. The status card shows only the screen name and states. Crash records stay on the device and are counted in a later report field, not uploaded.

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Build, dependencies and CI
text:
Build, dependencies and CI
**Build.** Gradle with the Kotlin DSL, a wrapper pinned with its distribution SHA-256, a version catalog, dependency locking and Gradle dependency verification with SHA-256 checksums for every artifact. Renovate updates the catalog.
**Toolchain.** JDK 17. `minSdk` 26 (Android 8.0), which gives `java.time`, current Keystore APIs and `java.nio.file` without desugaring. `compileSdk` and `targetSdk` follow the newest stable platform.
**Dependencies.** `core` uses Kotlin, kotlinx.serialization, OkHttp and Nimbus JOSE + JWT, and runs its own work on blocking calls and a two-thread download pool. `app` adds Media3 and the AndroidX libraries it needs. Tests use JUnit Jupiter and OkHttp's MockWebServer for `core`, and JUnit 4 with Robolectric for `app`.
**CI.** A `Player` job sets up JDK 17, validates the Gradle wrapper and runs `./gradlew check` on every pull request, joining the required gate. `core` needs only the JDK. `app` adds the Android SDK that GitHub's Ubuntu runners provide, and its unsigned release build. The root `pnpm validate` does not require Android tooling; `apps/player/README.md` lists the Gradle commands.
**Dependency hosts.** Building `app` needs Google's Maven repository, which redirects to `dl.google.com`. The current cloud development environment refuses that host ([PH-26](human-actions.md#ph-26)), so `app` can be written and verified only after it is allowed or on a developer machine. `core` builds with Maven Central and the Gradle plugin portal.

Decisions
The agent took these decisions on 2026-10-20 under the owner's delegation:
**Components.** One Gradle build in `apps/player` with a pure-JVM `core` holding every rule and an Android `app` holding the platform adapters (ADR-0031). It sits outside the pnpm workspace, is checked by its own required CI job and reads the repository's shared fixtures.
**Unattended operation.** The managed profile (device owner, HOME activity, lock task) is the supported pilot profile. The basic profile counts only where PH-08 shows boot and crash recovery.
**File-based state.** No database: write-once content-addressed media, exact manifests and one atomically replaced state record. Activation is a single replacement, and startup reconciliation is deterministic (ADR-0031).
**Credential vault.** AES-256-GCM under a non-exportable Android Keystore key, backup disabled. An unreadable vault means erase and enroll again.
**Server zone offsets.** The sync response carries the screen zone's offsets for 35 days, and the player never uses device time zone data for business time (ADR-0031).
**Trusted time.** A monotonic anchor from each sync, a persisted lower bound, and the system clock after a reboot only when it is not earlier than that bound and automatic network time is on; otherwise neutral output with `CLOCK_UNTRUSTED`.
**Authorization.** Keys pinned at pairing and refreshed over TLS only for an unknown `kid`. Only the latest verified statement counts. Protected output needs an unexpired statement listing the playing generation.
**Staging.** Strict protocol 1 parsing, preflight against the AT-05 reserve, at most two resumable downloads verified by length and SHA-256, superseding by newer desired publications, and activation immediately when ready.
**Playback.** ExoPlayer for images and videos with the next item prepared, fit without distortion, muted in protocol 1, schedule boundaries timed on the monotonic clock, and failed items skipped and reported.
**Updates.** Server-distributed APKs verified by SHA-256 and signing certificate, installed by the device owner inside a local window. No downgrade: rollback is a roll-forward release (ADR-0031).
**Platform floor.** `minSdk` 26 and JDK 17. Dependencies: Kotlin, kotlinx.serialization, OkHttp and Nimbus JOSE + JWT in `core`, and Media3 in `app`, all pinned and checksum-verified.
**Hardware envelope (2026-10-22, same delegation).** Certified Android TV or Google TV devices with Android 9 or later, Anatel homologation, 2 GB of RAM, 8 GB of storage and H.264 1080p30 hardware decoding. A Google TV HDMI device is the pilot's reference class. Uncertified TV boxes and non-Android smart TVs are excluded ([envelope](#supported-hardware-envelope)).

title: Teluni Android TV Player Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**Room or another database for local state.** Gives queries and transactions, but brings schema migrations that interact with the no-downgrade rule. Its write-ahead log still needs power-loss testing, and the state is a handful of pointers. Atomic file replacement is simpler to reason about and to fault-test.
**Device time zone data, or a bundled time zone library (ThreeTenBP, Joda-Time).** Device data can be years old on unmanaged TV boxes. A bundled database updates only with player releases and can still disagree with the server's preview. Offsets computed by the same server code that renders the preview cannot disagree, and need no dependency.
**A WebView or web player.** Reuses web skills, but leaves storage, autostart, power-loss behavior and hardware decoding to the browser on each device. ADR-0020 already chose a native player.
**Google Play distribution and in-app updates.** Requires store accounts, review and a Google account on each device. It does not give unattended updates inside a business window, and many commercial Android TV boxes do not have Play. It remains possible later for devices that do.
**A hand-written JWS verifier.** The format is small, but the policies forbid custom cryptographic schemes. Nimbus restricts algorithms, parses keys and handles the signature encoding with an established implementation.
**Starting at boot with a `BOOT_COMPLETED` receiver.** Android 10 and later block background activity starts without special permissions that TV devices often cannot grant. A device-owner HOME activity starts and restarts reliably.
**Certificate pinning for the API.** Would brick screens when the pilot host's certificate or provider changes. TLS with the system trust store plus pinned statement keys protects what matters offline.
